hyps.why: Edge 4 is only reachable through edge 0, so if edge 0 is none the conv on edge 4 is dead weight.
Edge 5 is fed by node 2, which is reached through edge 1 (or edges 0 and 2), so cutting edge 1 weakens the gain.
With edge 4 removed, edge 0 only reaches the output through the 0->1->2->3 route, so a conv there helps less.
Edge 1 feeds node 2, and with edge 5 removed node 2 cannot reach the output, so the conv is wasted.
Edge 2 only carries signal from node 1, which is dead when edge 0 is none.
Removing edge 4 costs little when edge 0 already makes it unreachable, so the effect is less negative.
Removing edge 5 hurts less when edge 1 is already none and the path through node 2 is weaker.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct edge adds a new path, so the gain is larger than when replacing an existing op.
A direct skip matters more when the other short path through node 1 is absent and few good routes remain.
Removing edge 2 is nearly harmless when edge 0 already disconnects node 1 from the input.
